description:
Goal

Reject an impossible resource field access while the settled receiver type and source span are authoritative. A known resource has the language-defined value projection, subject to opaque visibility; an arbitrary field such as h.foo is not a dynamic struct lookup.

Current root

LoweredStep::FieldAccess asks map_field_lookup. When a known resource has no requested atom field, semantic analysis currently replaces the failed lookup with any. That discards a proven impossibility. The invalid operation then reaches the backend interpreter as a runtime error and JIT/AOT as a host abort in fz_struct_get_named_field_ref.

Strategy

At semantic field resolution, distinguish a receiver domain that proves the field impossible from a genuinely unknown map or struct field set. Emit one stable source diagnostic with the field-access span for the impossible case. Preserve conservative any only for receivers whose settled domain can still support an unknown field. The runtime expect remains an unreachable compiler-invariant guard.

Acceptance

An in-module resource probe containing fn bad(h), do: h.foo is rejected consistently by interp, run, and build before backend execution, with the same diagnostic code and source span. h.value remains the payload projection. Resource lifecycle, file resource, file handle, and opaque payload fixtures remain green; library tests and strict clippy pass.
title: Reject impossible resource field access at the semantic boundary
